task_instance: Given a small Python source file (protocol.py) implementing a toy two-party authenticated key exchange (X25519 ECDH + HKDF + Ed25519 signing + ChaCha20-Poly1305 data transfer), run the skill's code-path workflow (grep for entry points, identify Initiator/Responder roles, trace message flow, annotate crypto ops, group into phases with an abort alt-block) and produce the required Mermaid sequenceDiagram markdown file plus verify it actually renders.
evidence: Created protocol.py (toy X25519/Ed25519/HKDF/ChaCha20-Poly1305 handshake). Ran the skill's Step-1 grep commands (rg-style patterns for handshake/keygen/round/send/recv and sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt/dh/kdf/hash) which correctly located the protocol entry points and crypto primitives. Manually executed Steps 2-7 to extract parties (Initiator, Responder), message flow (eph_I.pk ->, eph_R.pk+sig <-, ct ->), crypto annotations (keygen, DH, HKDF, Sign, Verify, Enc/Dec), phase grouping (Handshake/Init, Authentication/Key Derivation with an alt abort block, Data Transfer), and wrote the deliverable x25519-ed25519-ake-handshake.md containing the Mermaid sequenceDiagram plus the Protocol Summary section, matching the skill's required output structure. Verified the diagram is syntactically valid Mermaid by extracting the mermaid block to diagram.mmd and rendering it with @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli (npx mmdc -i diagram.mmd -o diagram.svg --puppeteer no-sandbox config), which produced a 197KB valid SVG sequence diagram document (role=graphics-document, aria-roledescription=sequence) containing both participant labels -- confirming the generated Mermaid actually renders correctly, not just looks plausible. Files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec/trailofbits__skills__crypto-protocol-diagram/{protocol.py, x25519-ed25519-ake-handshake.md, diagram.mmd, diagram.svg}. (An ASCII sequence diagram would also be printed inline per the skill's Step 7, which is a formatting/authoring step within Claude's own reach, not a runtime capability question, so it does not affect achievability.)
